geo_headlines: SPACEX REIGNITES THE AI TRADE. SpaceX, in its second quarter as a public company, reported revenue of $14.6 billion, up more than 160%, and a $4.4 billion profit; Musk said SpaceX and Tesla have formed committees to explore a merger (Yahoo Finance). SpaceX is up about 9% premarket. **S&P 500 futures 7,768.75 (+0.17%) and Nasdaq 100 futures 29,817.50 (+0.48%), with chip and memory ETFs up 1-3% (Investopedia).**

NETFLIX BEATS, CUTS AD FORECAST. Netflix earned $0.87 a share vs $0.82 expected on in-line revenue of $12.87 billion, but cut its 2026 ad revenue forecast to about $2.7 billion from $3 billion; shares are down about 6% (CNBC). Meta reports tonight as the first of the AI hyperscalers, with Tesla, IBM, Texas Instruments and Lam Research.

TUESDAY: THE DOW LED. The Dow rose 1.02% to 52,495.88 and the S&P 500 0.28% to 7,712.57, 1.36% below its October 6 record close; the Nasdaq 100 slipped 0.13%. 3M rose about 6%; GM fell about 7% despite its beat (Investopedia). VIX 17.31. The 10-year eased to 5.12%, the 30-year to 5.42% (Treasury). FedWatch as of Tuesday 10/20: October 16.6%, December 88.4%.

OIL: MINES IN HORMUZ. Brent $110.45 (+1.5%) and December WTI $99.57 (+1.8%). Iran's Revolutionary Guards said mines stopped three tankers on routes Tehran calls unauthorized, setting two ablaze (CNBC). The API estimated a 4.9 million barrel US crude draw (engine.online). Goldman says crude freight costs top $20 a barrel, about seven times a year ago (CNBC).

IRAN: STRAIT STAYS SHUT. Araghchi said Hormuz "will not be open to everyone" until an understanding is reached, with indirect talks continuing through Pakistan and Qatar (The National). Rubio called a deal "extremely difficult" and said economic pressure will continue (Al Jazeera). No US strikes on Iran were reported overnight.

ASIA REBOUNDS; EUROPE FLAT. Kospi +3.3% to 5,735.66 after a six-month closing low, led by Samsung and SK hynix (Trading Economics); Nikkei up about 1%. Stoxx 600 flat; Carrefour -12.5% after cutting its forecast on French riot costs, while EssilorLuxottica rose 11% (Reuters). The French-German 10-year spread widened past 155bp (Bloomberg).

TODAY. VIX options and futures expire this morning. 10:30 AM: EIA weekly oil inventories. Before the open: AT&T, Abbott, NextEra, CME, Thermo Fisher, Philip Morris (Earnings Whispers). After the close: Meta, Tesla, IBM, Texas Instruments, Lam Research. Thursday: jobless claims; P&G, Union Pacific. Fed quiet period before October 27-28.
client_frame_short: The AI story got a boost overnight: SpaceX's results showed AI spending turning into real revenue and profit, and Nasdaq futures are up. **Tonight Meta, the first of the big AI spenders to report, and Tesla will tell us much more than any headline about whether last week's worries were overdone.** Oil is back near $110 as Iran keeps Hormuz closed, but stocks have held up as earnings come in solid. For clients, the plan does not change: stay diversified, rebalance, and let results, not headlines, drive decisions.
client_frame:
If a client calls this morning, the story is that earnings are doing the heavy lifting while oil stays high.

Tuesday: the Dow rose 1% and the S&P 500 0.3%, while the Nasdaq slipped. Leadership rotated toward industrials such as 3M, a sign of a broadening market rather than a narrow tech one. The S&P 500 is about 1.4% below its October 6 record close.

Overnight: SpaceX reported revenue up more than 160% and a $4.4 billion profit, driven by AI and satellite internet. Elon Musk said SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a merger. That eased worries that AI spending will not pay off, and Nasdaq futures are higher. Netflix beat on profit but cut its advertising outlook, and its stock is down about 6%.

Tonight is the key test: Meta is the first of the big AI spenders to report, and Tesla reports too. Investors will judge whether AI investment is producing returns. Big single-day moves are common after these reports, in both directions, and rarely change long-term outcomes.

Oil: Brent is about $110. Iran says Hormuz stays closed until the US accepts its terms, and mines halted three tankers on Tuesday. Talks continue through Pakistan and Qatar, but Secretary Rubio called a deal extremely difficult. High oil keeps inflation sticky, and markets price about an 88% chance of a December Fed hike.

Why it matters: corporate results have been solid, which is what ultimately drives stock prices. Bonds paying about 5% give balanced portfolios a cushion while the oil story plays out.

For clients: stay invested, rebalance toward targets, and avoid trading on a single earnings report. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (Tuesday 5.12%), a 30-year above 5.75% (Tuesday 5.42%), or US strikes on Iran that keep Brent well above $105 (now $110.45). Brent is there; strikes are the missing piece.
